questions.title: Time, Speed & Distance — Train Crossing
questions.question: A train 150 meters long passes a pole in 15 seconds and another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.explanation: Speed of first train = 150 / 15 = 10 m/s. Combined relative speed = (150 + 150) / 12 = 25 m/s. Therefore, speed of second train = 25 - 10 = 15 m/s.

questions.title: Work & Pipes
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, Pipe B in 15 hours, and Pipe C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Net part filled per hour = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10. Thus, the tank will be full in 10 hours.

questions.title: Probability — Dice Sum
questions.question: Two unbiased dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum greater than 9?
questions.explanation: Favorable outcomes for sum > 9 (i.e. 10, 11, 12): (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6) = 6 outcomes. Total outcomes = 36. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.title: Time Complexity — Binary Search
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Binary Search on a sorted array of N elements?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the search space, resulting in at most log2(N) steps, or O(log N).

questions.title: Graph Algorithms — Dijkstra Limitation
questions.question: Why does Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
options: It uses DFS instead of BFS
Its greedy assumption that once a node is finalized its shortest distance cannot be improved breaks with negative edges
Priority queues cannot store negative integers
It only works on directed acyclic graphs
questions.explanation: Dijkstra greedily marks the minimum-distance unvisited node as finalized; a later negative edge could yield a shorter path, violating the greedy invariant.

questions.title: Data Structures — LRU Cache
questions.question: Which combination of data structures gives O(1) time complexity for both get() and put() in an LRU Cache?
questions.explanation: A Hash Map provides O(1) key lookup to nodes, while a Doubly Linked List allows O(1) removal and insertion at the head/tail.

questions.title: SQL — WHERE vs HAVING
questions.question: Which clause is used to filter aggregated groups produced by GROUP BY in SQL?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) are computed.

questions.title: DBMS — BCNF vs 3NF
questions.question: A relation is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) if and only if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y:
options: There are no transitive dependencies only
questions.explanation: BCNF strictly requires that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, the determinant X must be a superkey.

questions.title: SQL — Second Highest Salary
questions.question: Which query reliably returns the second highest distinct salary from an Employee table?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee)
SELECT COUNT(salary) FROM Employee GROUP BY salary
questions.explanation: Comparing against the subquery (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee) finds the maximum salary strictly less than the highest salary.

questions.title: OS — Virtual Memory & Thrashing
questions.question: Which condition directly causes Thrashing in an Operating System?

questions.title: Time, Speed & Distance — Train Crossing
questions.question: A train 150 meters long passes a pole in 15 seconds and another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.explanation: Speed of first train = 150 / 15 = 10 m/s. Combined relative speed = (150 + 150) / 12 = 25 m/s. Therefore, speed of second train = 25 - 10 = 15 m/s.

questions.title: Work & Pipes
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, Pipe B in 15 hours, and Pipe C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Net part filled per hour = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10. Thus, the tank will be full in 10 hours.

questions.title: Probability — Dice Sum
questions.question: Two unbiased dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum greater than 9?
questions.explanation: Favorable outcomes for sum > 9 (i.e. 10, 11, 12): (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6) = 6 outcomes. Total outcomes = 36. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.title: Time Complexity — Binary Search
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Binary Search on a sorted array of N elements?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the search space, resulting in at most log2(N) steps, or O(log N).

questions.question: Why does Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
options: It uses DFS instead of BFS
Its greedy assumption that once a node is finalized its shortest distance cannot be improved breaks with negative edges
Priority queues cannot store negative integers
It only works on directed acyclic graphs
questions.explanation: Dijkstra greedily marks the minimum-distance unvisited node as finalized; a later negative edge could yield a shorter path, violating the greedy invariant.

questions.title: Data Structures — LRU Cache
questions.question: Which combination of data structures gives O(1) time complexity for both get() and put() in an LRU Cache?
questions.explanation: A Hash Map provides O(1) key lookup to nodes, while a Doubly Linked List allows O(1) removal and insertion at the head/tail.

questions.title: SQL — WHERE vs HAVING
questions.question: Which clause is used to filter aggregated groups produced by GROUP BY in SQL?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) are computed.

questions.title: DBMS — BCNF vs 3NF
questions.question: A relation is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) if and only if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y:
options: There are no transitive dependencies only
questions.explanation: BCNF strictly requires that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, the determinant X must be a superkey.

questions.title: SQL — Second Highest Salary
questions.question: Which query reliably returns the second highest distinct salary from an Employee table?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee)
SELECT COUNT(salary) FROM Employee GROUP BY salary
questions.explanation: Comparing against the subquery (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee) finds the maximum salary strictly less than the highest salary.

questions.title: OS — Virtual Memory & Thrashing
questions.question: Which condition directly causes Thrashing in an Operating System?
options: Excessive paging activity where CPU spends more time swapping pages than executing
Round Robin time quantum being too large
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the working set of active processes exceeds physical RAM, causing continuous page faults and swapping.

questions.title: Computer Networks — TCP Congestion Control
questions.question: During TCP Slow Start, how does the congestion window (cwnd) grow on each received ACK before reaching ssthresh?
questions.explanation: In TCP Slow Start, cwnd increases by 1 MSS per ACK received, which results in exponential doubling every Round-Trip Time (RTT).

questions.title: OOP — Runtime Polymorphism
questions.question: In C++ / Java, how is runtime polymorphism (dynamic method dispatch) achieved?
questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism is resolved at runtime via virtual method tables (vtable) when a base class reference points to a derived class object.

questions.title: Are web development projects valued during mass and premium IT drives?
questions.content: I have built a couple of MERN stack projects. Will interviewers ask me to write React code or do they strictly stick to DSA and Java/C++?

seniorProfile.bio: AWS Cloud Engineer. Mentor for system architecture, operating systems, distributed storage, and behavioral STAR interviews.
seniorProfile.expertiseTopics: Cloud, AWS, Microservices, DBMS, OOP, Behavioral Rounds

answers.content: Yes, absolutely! Having full-stack projects gives you something tangible to drive the interview discussion. They will ask how your APIs communicate, how state is managed, how you handled database schema design, and how you secured user passwords. Be ready to explain your architecture on paper.

questions.title: How should a 3rd year student structure daily preparation for Tier-1 companies?
questions.content: Hi Priya, I am currently in 6th semester. I find it difficult to balance semester college exams with LeetCode. How many hours did you dedicate daily, and what roadmap would you suggest?

seniorProfile.bio: SDE at Microsoft Cloud Azure Core. Specializing in high-throughput backend services, LeetCode data structures, and helping juniors navigate technical interview rounds.
seniorProfile.expertiseTopics: DSA, System Design, Graph Algorithms, Dynamic Programming, Core CS

answers.content: Hi Aarav! Consistency beats marathon weekend sessions. Dedicate 2 focused hours daily: 1 hour for 1-2 coding problems (aim for quality over quantity, understand patterns), and 1 hour for Core CS subjects (DBMS, OS, Networks). During exam months, drop coding to 3-4 problems a week and focus on academics, since maintaining a 7.5+ CGPA is a mandatory cutoff for Microsoft, Cisco, and Goldman Sachs.

questions.title: Time, Speed & Distance — Train Crossing
questions.question: A train 150 meters long passes a pole in 15 seconds and another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.explanation: Speed of first train = 150 / 15 = 10 m/s. Combined relative speed = (150 + 150) / 12 = 25 m/s. Therefore, speed of second train = 25 - 10 = 15 m/s.

questions.title: Work & Pipes
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, Pipe B in 15 hours, and Pipe C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Net part filled per hour = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10. Thus, the tank will be full in 10 hours.

questions.title: Probability — Dice Sum
questions.question: Two unbiased dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum greater than 9?
questions.explanation: Favorable outcomes for sum > 9 (i.e. 10, 11, 12): (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6) = 6 outcomes. Total outcomes = 36. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.title: Time Complexity — Binary Search
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Binary Search on a sorted array of N elements?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the search space, resulting in at most log2(N) steps, or O(log N).

questions.title: Graph Algorithms — Dijkstra Limitation
questions.question: Why does Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
options: It uses DFS instead of BFS
Its greedy assumption that once a node is finalized its shortest distance cannot be improved breaks with negative edges
Priority queues cannot store negative integers
It only works on directed acyclic graphs
questions.explanation: Dijkstra greedily marks the minimum-distance unvisited node as finalized; a later negative edge could yield a shorter path, violating the greedy invariant.

questions.title: Data Structures — LRU Cache
questions.question: Which combination of data structures gives O(1) time complexity for both get() and put() in an LRU Cache?
questions.explanation: A Hash Map provides O(1) key lookup to nodes, while a Doubly Linked List allows O(1) removal and insertion at the head/tail.

questions.title: SQL — WHERE vs HAVING
questions.question: Which clause is used to filter aggregated groups produced by GROUP BY in SQL?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) are computed.

questions.title: DBMS — BCNF vs 3NF
questions.question: A relation is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) if and only if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y:
options: There are no transitive dependencies only
questions.explanation: BCNF strictly requires that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, the determinant X must be a superkey.

questions.title: SQL — Second Highest Salary
questions.question: Which query reliably returns the second highest distinct salary from an Employee table?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee)
SELECT COUNT(salary) FROM Employee GROUP BY salary
questions.explanation: Comparing against the subquery (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee) finds the maximum salary strictly less than the highest salary.

questions.title: OS — Virtual Memory & Thrashing
questions.question: Which condition directly causes Thrashing in an Operating System?
options: Excessive paging activity where CPU spends more time swapping pages than executing
Round Robin time quantum being too large
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the working set of active processes exceeds physical RAM, causing continuous page faults and swapping.

questions.title: Computer Networks — TCP Congestion Control
questions.question: During TCP Slow Start, how does the congestion window (cwnd) grow on each received ACK before reaching ssthresh?
questions.explanation: In TCP Slow Start, cwnd increases by 1 MSS per ACK received, which results in exponential doubling every Round-Trip Time (RTT).

questions.title: OOP — Runtime Polymorphism
questions.question: In C++ / Java, how is runtime polymorphism (dynamic method dispatch) achieved?
questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism is resolved at runtime via virtual method tables (vtable) when a base class reference points to a derived class object.

questions.title: Are web development projects valued during mass and premium IT drives?
questions.content: I have built a couple of MERN stack projects. Will interviewers ask me to write React code or do they strictly stick to DSA and Java/C++?

seniorProfile.bio: AWS Cloud Engineer. Mentor for system architecture, operating systems, distributed storage, and behavioral STAR interviews.
seniorProfile.expertiseTopics: Cloud, AWS, Microservices, DBMS, OOP, Behavioral Rounds

answers.content: Yes, absolutely! Having full-stack projects gives you something tangible to drive the interview discussion. They will ask how your APIs communicate, how state is managed, how you handled database schema design, and how you secured user passwords. Be ready to explain your architecture on paper.

questions.content: Hi Priya, I am currently in 6th semester. I find it difficult to balance semester college exams with LeetCode. How many hours did you dedicate daily, and what roadmap would you suggest?

answers.content: Hi Aarav! Consistency beats marathon weekend sessions. questions.title: Time, Speed & Distance — Train Crossing
questions.question: A train 150 meters long passes a pole in 15 seconds and another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.explanation: Speed of first train = 150 / 15 = 10 m/s. Combined relative speed = (150 + 150) / 12 = 25 m/s. Therefore, speed of second train = 25 - 10 = 15 m/s.

questions.title: Work & Pipes
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, Pipe B in 15 hours, and Pipe C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Net part filled per hour = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10. Thus, the tank will be full in 10 hours.

questions.title: Probability — Dice Sum
questions.question: Two unbiased dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum greater than 9?
questions.explanation: Favorable outcomes for sum > 9 (i.e. 10, 11, 12): (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6) = 6 outcomes. Total outcomes = 36. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.title: Time Complexity — Binary Search
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Binary Search on a sorted array of N elements?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the search space, resulting in at most log2(N) steps, or O(log N).

questions.title: Graph Algorithms — Dijkstra Limitation
questions.question: Why does Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
options: It uses DFS instead of BFS
Its greedy assumption that once a node is finalized its shortest distance cannot be improved breaks with negative edges
Priority queues cannot store negative integers
It only works on directed acyclic graphs
questions.explanation: Dijkstra greedily marks the minimum-distance unvisited node as finalized; a later negative edge could yield a shorter path, violating the greedy invariant.

questions.title: Data Structures — LRU Cache
questions.question: Which combination of data structures gives O(1) time complexity for both get() and put() in an LRU Cache?
questions.explanation: A Hash Map provides O(1) key lookup to nodes, while a Doubly Linked List allows O(1) removal and insertion at the head/tail.

questions.title: SQL — WHERE vs HAVING
questions.question: Which clause is used to filter aggregated groups produced by GROUP BY in SQL?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) are computed.

questions.title: DBMS — BCNF vs 3NF
questions.question: A relation is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) if and only if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y:
options: There are no transitive dependencies only
questions.explanation: BCNF strictly requires that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, the determinant X must be a superkey.

questions.title: SQL — Second Highest Salary
questions.question: Which query reliably returns the second highest distinct salary from an Employee table?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee)
SELECT COUNT(salary) FROM Employee GROUP BY salary
questions.explanation: Comparing against the subquery (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee) finds the maximum salary strictly less than the highest salary.

questions.title: OS — Virtual Memory & Thrashing
questions.question: Which condition directly causes Thrashing in an Operating System?
options: Excessive paging activity where CPU spends more time swapping pages than executing
Round Robin time quantum being too large
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the working set of active processes exceeds physical RAM, causing continuous page faults and swapping.

questions.title: Computer Networks — TCP Congestion Control
questions.question: During TCP Slow Start, how does the congestion window (cwnd) grow on each received ACK before reaching ssthresh?
questions.explanation: In TCP Slow Start, cwnd increases by 1 MSS per ACK received, which results in exponential doubling every Round-Trip Time (RTT).

questions.title: OOP — Runtime Polymorphism
questions.question: In C++ / Java, how is runtime polymorphism (dynamic method dispatch) achieved?
questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism is resolved at runtime via virtual method tables (vtable) when a base class reference points to a derived class object.

answers.content: Hi Aarav! Consistency beats marathon weekend sessions. Dedicate 2 focused hours daily: 1 hour for 1-2 coding problems (aim for quality over quantity, understand patterns), and 1 hour for Core CS subjects (DBMS, OS, Networks). During exam months, drop coding to 3-4 problems a week and focus on academics, since maintaining a 7.5+ CGPA is a mandatory cutoff for Microsoft, Cisco, and Goldman Sachs.
